rationale: Use own colour and the column's nonzero colour set. In demonstration 1, column 1 contains {1,2}, and both colours become 8; column 3 contains {2,3}, and its 3s become 9. Other keys retain their colours.

Column sets determine the substitutions: {1,3} maps 0 to 5; {1,2,3} maps 0 to 8 and 2 to 7; {2,3} maps 2 to 0. Demonstration 2 shows all three column types, including column 1's zeros becoming 5 and column 6's 2s becoming 0.
Use column colour sets: {1,3} maps 0 to 2, {1,2} maps 2 to 9, and {1,2,3} maps 1 to 0. Demonstration 1 exhibits these respectively in columns 1, 3, and 5.

Use the complete 3x3 neighbourhood including outside-grid markers. Demonstration 6 changes the top-left zero to 6 where its right, lower, and lower-right neighbours are all zero; the remaining demonstrated neighbourhoods preserve their centre colours.
Use complete 3x3 neighbourhoods. Demonstrations 6 and 8 change the top-right zero to 4 when the left, lower-left, and lower neighbours are all zero, with outside-grid markers identifying the corner.
Column set {1,3} maps 0 to 4; {3} maps 0 to 9; {1,2,3} maps both 0 and 3 to 6. Demonstration 3 shows these in columns 2, 1, and 3 respectively.

Use own colour and directional nearest nonzero colours. In demonstration 5, the first two zeros in column 1 have no nonzero above or left, 3 below, and 1 right, and both become 5. Demonstration 6's bottom-row zeros between 3s become 8.

Use full 3x3 patterns with boundary markers. Demonstration 6 changes row 2, column 4 to 2 for its all-zero in-grid neighbourhood at the right edge. Demonstration 10 changes row 4, column 4 to 4 where the same right-edge neighbourhood has a 1 directly below.
Use own colour and border flag. Every demonstration maps border colours 0,1,2,3 to 5,6,1,9 respectively while preserving interior pixels; demonstration 1 shows all four border substitutions.

Use own colour with both row and column nonzero sets. In demonstration 2, 2 becomes 4 at intersections of rows containing {1,2,3} and columns containing {2,3}; zeros become 4 where rows contain {1,2} and columns contain {2,3}. Demonstration 6 also supplies the distinct zero-to-9 key at row 2, column 4.
